result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both give plausible numbers, cap growth on big monitors and make code and tables scroll inside their own box. B keeps docs and marketing on one clearly tokenized set of widths (measure, content, wide, docs-main), and its explicit pricing column counts avoid orphaned cards. A has the richer table handling, including the sticky first column, but it repeats literal values such as 90rem, 72rem and 17rem instead of using its tokens, and it lists a 40rem breakpoint it never uses. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give plausible values and a named-line grid with prose, wide and full tracks, and both have code and tables scroll inside their own box. A is more disciplined: nearly every width is a named token, the docs shell width is built from those tokens, and the pricing grid avoids a lone card on its own row. B hard-codes 72rem and 90rem even though it defines --page-max, and it adds extras like heading sizes and sticky table columns. B's notes on mid-size docs columns and big monitors are useful, but its auto-fit pricing grid can leave a lone card on the last row.
